notes: The world keeps its own clock now. Wall time was never the right clock for a story — play happens in bursts, and a week of not opening the app is not a week in anyone's life — so there is a story datetime that moves only when you play or when you say so. Every message is stamped with it, and with whether you were texting or together at the time. The bar at the top of a chat is now that clock: 'Tuesday evening, 9:00 PM · in person'. Tapping it moves time (quarter of an hour, an hour, later tonight, next morning, next day), sets whether you are texting or together, and names where you are — and writes a dated line into the transcript so that part of the conversation is pinned to when it happened. Go see them does the whole move in one tap: half an hour passes, you are in person, and it is marked. Ordinary play drifts the clock a few minutes a turn, so you rarely touch it; switching between chats costs nothing, so you can text three people in the same afternoon. Characters read all of this: on Wednesday morning Harper knows you were together last night while Erin knows you texted her yesterday afternoon, both in the same words a person would use. Nothing already in your history moves — the clock was seeded from the real one, so old conversations keep the times they already had.
